mostWorthwhile.text: Using ATP to run the sodium-potassium pump was most worthwhile: it connected making ATP to a visible job and showed sodium moving out despite its inward pull.

leastWorthwhile.text: The mitochondrial electron-transfer picture was the hardest passage to follow. It showed the route to ATP, but the electron carriers and proton gradient were not very familiar.

surprise.text: I was surprised that breaking down glucose produced ATP without an oxygen input, while the later mitochondrial route used oxygen and formed water.

arbitrary.text: No action felt entirely purposeless, but supplying pyruvate to the mitochondrion followed the picture's arrow before I understood what the electron carriers would do.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter: connecting ATP production to the pump and protein-making was satisfying, though I would want more explanation of the unfamiliar molecular details.
